messages:
maria_support: FYI — incoming from ACME (org-acme). They say their monthly credits dropped to 0 mid-day and clients started getting 429s. They insist they didn't exceed expected traffic. Link to customer logs in the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-4321

aj_ops: can you paste the 429 response headers? usually `X-RateLimit-Remaining` etc. If it's quota exhaustion vs rate limiting we handle differently.

maria_support: pasted from their repro log:```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 13:12:45 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 0
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 165
Retry-After: 165
{ "error": "quota_exhausted", "message": "monthly credits exhausted for org-acme" }```

sam_infra: X-RateLimit-Limit: 0 is our quota-exhaustion sentinel in the hosted billing flow. Means billing mark set to 0 tokens available. Not a transient per-minute rate limit.

jenna_customer_success: Customer says they run batch jobs nightly and always have a burst cushion. They saw the drop around 05:00 local (PDT) which is ~12:00 UTC. They suspect DST or timezone misalignment.

tim_billing: quick context: monthly credit refills run in the billing service at 00:05 UTC on the customer's billing cycle start date. We batch-process reconciliations and then set the org credit counter. DST/locale does not shift the UTC refill time. If their account cycle starts on the 15th, refill is at 00:05 UTC on the 15th.

maria_support: Could this be a misapplied proration or a failed refill job?

sam_infra: Checking billing job runs now. `kubectl -n billing logs -l app=billing-worker --since=24h | grep org-acme`
sam_infra: Job ran at 00:05 UTC on the 15th and returned success for org-acme: `credited 500000 tokens`. No errors.

aj_ops: If they were credited, why did they hit 0 later? Two theories: 1) unexpected heavy usage (bot loop) burned tokens after refill. 2) client-side SDK or proxy double-sending requests (retries without backoff), or 3) credits consumed by background embeddings or long-chained completions.

maria_support: I've asked customer for top request IDs and a short timeframe. They sent a sample: `req_8f7c2a` at 12:08 UTC.

sam_infra: I pulled the request trace: `req_8f7c2a` = series of ~1300 small completions during a 3 minute window from a single IP. Looks like a batch job that didn't use streaming batching and sent many short prompts. That can burn tokens fast.

jenna_customer_success: Customer insists their nightly job hasn't changed for months. Could a recent SDK update change batching behavior? They upgraded from `redwood-sdk@1.6.2` to `@1.7.0` last week.

aj_ops: Good catch. `1.7.0` defaulted to `max_tokens_per_call` smaller and switched off some implicit micro-batching. That can increase token and request counts. We should repro locally.

maria_support: Action items so far: 1) Offer emergency top-up so their production remains online. 2) Diagnose exact token burn and root cause. 3) If SDK change is culprit, give mitigation steps.

tim_billing: I can apply a one-off emergency allocation of 200k tokens to org-acme if CS approves. Will need a billing ticket and an approval note.

jenna_customer_success: I'll ring the customer and get approval for an emergency credit. If they accept, please apply and I'll confirm.

quota-bot: Automated alert: org-acme monthly quota exhausted at 2026-07-15T12:08:21Z — notifications sent to billing and support channels. Ticket CS-4321 created.

sam_infra: For repro, here's a curl that shows the 429 they saw (we ran it against sandbox):```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"open-7b", "prompt":"x", "max_tokens":16}'
```
If you repeat that 1000x without batching you'll see similar exhaustion.

aj_ops: Suggest we add a short-term guard on org-acme to block runaway parallelism: set `concurrency_limit=30` and enable `soft_throttle=true` for them in the routing layer. That prevents another mid-day outage while we investigate.

sam_infra: I can apply that for 2 hours. Doing it now.

sam_infra: Applied `concurrency_limit=30` and `soft_throttle=true` for org-acme. Monitoring for denied request surge.

maria_support: Customer accepted emergency top-up; tim_billing, please proceed.

tim_billing: Applied emergency allocation +200000 tokens to org-acme. Note: this is a ledger adjustment flagged as "emergency support credit". Will reconcile on monthly invoice.

jenna_customer_success: Customer online, confirmed requests now succeeding. Thanks team.

maria_support: Next steps: - aj_ops to confirm SDK 1.7.0 behavior and produce a short KB for customers and SDK changelog entry. - support to advise ACME to pin to 1.6.x or to enable batching/streaming in their job. - billing to note the emergency credit and follow up on invoicing. - infra to keep the temporary concurrency limit for 24h and then evaluate.

aj_ops: I'll open an internal PR and a short KB: "Unexpected token burn after SDK 1.7.0 due to micro-batching change". Include repro steps and recommended config (enable streaming, or set `batch_size: 64`/`concurrency_limit: 10`).

tim_billing: Logging CS-4321 -> Billing action required: emergency credit + reconciliation note.

maria_support: Closing loop — customer happy for now. Leaving thread open for postmortem notes.

sam_infra: Postmortem checklist: collect token consumption timeline (per-minute), SDK version, IPs, request shapes, and confirm no billing job failures. I'll dump the metrics at EOD.

jenna_customer_success: I'll schedule a customer follow-up next week to review usage patterns and propose Dedicated or Reserved capacity if they need predictable monthly throughput.

maria_support: Thanks all :heart:
